status: draft after the second round of checks after pilot 1 (18.11.2026): ready for the second development pilot; to be frozen after it and the project lead's decisions
claim: for q0b_3 only (chosen after a screening on the development sample): whether the firm profile adds checkable information about the firm's own answer to this contemporaneous survey question over the segmentation (size and sector) given to the SAME model (H1), and, secondarily, over a statistical size x sector segmentation learned on the development sample (H3); not a prediction of future behaviour, not a validation of interest in a new product

data.source: EC/ECB SAFE public use file, Polish records
data.development: waves 2024Q3 and 2025Q3 without any observation of a firm in the test wave

question.additional: qa21 (late payments from private entities), separate build, same rules

analysis_population: firms that answered q0b_3 with 1-10; 'don't know / not applicable' (99) not asked, counted and reported

methods.llm_shuffled: own size and sector, the other block from a donor of the same size x sector cell ('shuffled'); diagnostic
methods.marginal: the distribution of the ten answers in the training data, +0.5 per value
methods.rule: size x sector cell distribution smoothed toward the marginal with weight 10
methods.logit: L2 multinomial logit on the 25 card columns of the card key (safe_signal_check.CARD; 6 structural, 11 sources of financing, 4 applications, 4 outcomes), ten values; penalty chosen from (0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3) by 4-fold cross-validation grouped by firm on the training data, by the band log-loss floored as in the final comparison (since 0.7: the same scoring function as the report; before, the cross-validation scored without the floor and could rank two penalties the other way); every fit must converge
methods.logit_segment: the same procedure on size and sector only: the statistical counterpart of llm_segment (the size x sector rule is worse than the marginal on the development sample, so it is not the best use of these two fields)
methods.logit_without_applications: the logit without q7a and q7b (explanatory ablation: how much signal comes from applications and their outcomes)

training_data_of_the_statistical_methods.development_pilot: the development sample without the pilot's firms

models: the three model configurations of the B-K2 panel, each in its own run: local Qwen (qwen3.8:27b on Ollama 0.40.15, digest recorded by the runner), Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5), GPT-6 Luna (gpt-6-luna); to fill before freezing: the exact dated version ids the APIs report (served_model in the answers) and each model's stated training cutoff

probabilities.elicitation: since 0.4: the model gives, for 100 firms with an identical card, how many would choose each rating 1-10 (integers 0-100; the sum need not be 100, the counts are turned into shares by the parser, as the prompt says). The first pilot asked for probabilities summing to 1 (tolerance 0.02): 88 of Qwen's 90 invalid attempts failed only on the sum, concentrated on the short card (34/120 final errors), so the sum rule tested arithmetic, not the distribution; the counts format removes that arithmetic by construction instead of widening the tolerance to pass the seen answers; since 0.5 a zero is allowed ("prawie żadna z tych firm"; the scoring floor prevents an infinite log-loss) and the 100 firms are defined as firms in Poland known only through the card
probabilities.parser: safe_prompt.parse_counts: one JSON object with keys firms_per_100 (keys 1..10, integers 0-100, not all 0) and reason; anything else is a technical error
probabilities.floor: every method's ten probabilities p are scored as (1 - 0.01) p + 0.01 / 10
probabilities.sums: F4: every sum > 0 is valid; the report gives the raw sums by model and variant (share exactly 100, outside 80-120 and outside 50-200, min, median, max); a sensitivity treats answers with a sum outside 50-200 as technical errors, on equal footing with the main result when they exceed 5% of a model's answers

technical_errors: a refusal, a cut or an answer the parser rejects is asked again in a fresh conversation, up to 2 model attempts; still without a valid answer: a technical error, never a survey answer. Main analysis on the common denominator of each comparison; counts by outcome reported. Sensitivities: technical errors scored with the marginal; scored worst in both arms (symmetric); scored against the claim (a failed full card worst, a failed segment card with the marginal). If a model has more than 5% technical errors in any variant (flag in the report), the main result and the sensitivities are reported on equal footing, with the difference of error shares between full and segment and its bootstrap interval; F5: with differential errors (the bootstrap interval of the full - segment error-share difference excludes 0) or over 5% in a variant, only the against-the-claim sensitivity stands on equal footing with the main result (the symmetric worst case then favours the claim: Qwen in pilot 1, d = +1.34)
main_measure: band log-loss per firm (natural log), lower is better; the log score is its negative

primary_family.comparisons: for each of the three models: llm_full vs llm_segment
primary_family.statistic: the mean over firms of d = log score(full) - log score(segment)
primary_family.test: two-sided studentised bootstrap test (bootstrap-t) of mean d = 0, 10,000 resamples of firms with a fixed seed; the sign-flip permutation test and the t test are reported next to it. Reason (since 0.4): the sign-flip test is exact only if d is symmetric about 0 under the null (or under an exchangeability null), which equal mean log scores do not imply; in the simulation (scripts/safe_test_level_sim.py, data/processed/safe_test_level_sim_v0.1.json) at n = 692 it rejected a true null in 6.6% at 0.05 and 3.0% at 0.05/3 for strongly skewed d, the bootstrap-t in 6.1% and 2.1% (normal d: all about nominal); the report also gives the skewness of d and, with --level-check, the level of the bootstrap-t on the model's own centred differences, so the remaining liberalness under skew is visible; since 0.6 the interval is the symmetric studentised bootstrap interval m +- q95(|t*|) se from the same resamples as the test (an equal-tailed studentised interval could exclude 0 while the two-sided test did not reject; the symmetric one excludes 0 exactly when the test rejects at 0.05, up to the +1 in the p value; the percentile interval is liberal under skew and reported only as auxiliary), a comparison with fewer than 30 common firms gets no test (p None), and p values are directional (p if the mean difference > 0, else 1)
primary_family.multiplicity: decided by the project lead (19.11.2026), before the confirmatory analysis: Holm over the three H1 (full vs segment, one per model) at alpha 0.05, with the directional rule unchanged (p if the mean d > 0, else 1). The choice between the graph (Bretz et al. 2009, H1 and H3) and Holm over H1 was open in the plan; it is made now, after the development results, and is described as such: the calibration of H3 was not confirmed for two models in the third pilot, and in the graph a rejected H3 passes its level on to the other H1, so the limitation would not stay with H3. No model's results were selected. (Until 19.11.2026: the graph, alpha/3 on each H1, H1_i -> H3_i weight 1, H3_i -> H1_j weight 1/2.)
primary_family.interval: since 0.6: the symmetric 95% studentised bootstrap interval of the mean d (m +- q95(|t*|) se, the resamples of the test; none below 30 common firms); the 95% percentile interval (2,000 resamples) only as auxiliary
primary_family.claim_scope: a rejected H1 supports 'the profile helps this model over its own segmentation'; a rejected H3 supports 'over a statistical size x sector segmentation'; per model only; one model's result is not a conclusion about all three
primary_family.missing: a model without a common firm, or absent from the report, enters Holm with p = 1 (flagged)

mandatory_references: for every model the differences full - marginal and segment - marginal are reported next to the main comparison: the full card can improve a weak segment variant and still be worse than the plain answer distribution
explanatory: rule and logit (distance of each LLM variant to them)
full vs shuffled (information about this firm vs a description of a typical firm)
ten-value log-loss and the ranked probability score (RPS)
calibration: mean predicted band probability vs observed band share, by band and by size class
stability: the repeated full card on a fixed subsample (mean absolute difference of the ten probabilities and of the band log score)
frozen_before_test: the dated model version ids and their settings
K of the precision rule and the technical-error rule
the logit's field list (the card key)
the main test (bootstrap-t) and its resamples
the graph of H1 and H3 (or Holm over H1, by the project lead's decision)
the sums rule F4 and the equal-footing rule F5
K per model and the averaging of log scores
estimand: since 0.7: the unweighted mean of d over the Polish 2026Q3 SAFE respondents answering q0b_3 with 1-10 (the sample, not the population of firms) WHO HAVE ALL K DRAWS OF BOTH CARDS VALID for that model (complete cases at the frozen K); the coverage (complete cases / eligible respondents, overall and by size class) and the technical-error sensitivities over all eligible respondents are reported next to it as mandatory; decided by the project lead (18.11.2026): the main claim is about these complete cases only, not extended to all eligible firms or to the population of Polish firms; if the against-the-claim sensitivity gives a different picture, the dependence of the conclusion on the missing answers is described; results weighted with wgtcommon only as explanatory
null_result_reporting: a non-rejection is reported with the interval of the mean d: 'the full card improves the band log score by less than X nats' with X the upper bound

interpretation_table.H1 rejected (d > 0), full - shuffled int: indication (descriptive) that matching the other features to this firm improves the score
interpretation_table.H1 rejected, full - shuffled interval in: not established whether matching the other features to this firm improves the score (not evidence that it does not)
interpretation_table.H1 rejected, full - shuffled interval be: the features matched to the firm do worse than a donor's (descriptive)
interpretation_table.H1 rejected, the segment card below the: the advantage of the full card may be a repair of the model's weak starting point, not an advantage over simple segmentation; H3 and the reference with the marginal decide that
interpretation_table.H1 rejected, full below the marginal (in: the profile helps a weak segment variant while the model loses to the plain answer distribution
interpretation_table.H1 not rejected: reported by null_result_reporting: the full card improves the band log score by less than the upper bound of the interval

secondary_gated: withdrawn in 0.4: testing full vs shuffled only for the models selected by the primary result, with Holm among them, does not control the error by itself (a hierarchical procedure would need a defined transfer of alpha between the families); full vs shuffled is diagnostic (interval, no test, no claim)
explanatory_rules: explanatory analyses give no p values or claims; their intervals are unadjusted and described as descriptive; the split by size class (4 x 3 models) is descriptive; floor sensitivities 0.001 and 0.05 explanatory only
precision_from_the_pilot: the development pilot reports per model: SD and mean of d by size class and, since 0.7, the total SD of d over the test wave's size shares (within-class variances plus the spread of the class means, the variance the unstratified bootstrap of the test sees; before, the between-class part was left out and the MDE could be several times too small), with n = the sum over size classes of 692 x the test share of the class x the run's coverage in that class at its K, and the variance over the size mix of that retained sample (since 0.7; a mean coverage would be too optimistic when the coverage differs between classes and the class shares differ between the pilot and the test); the minimum detectable effect at 80% power for alpha 0.05/3 and 0.05 with 692 firms, the share of the variance of d from model randomness (repeats), the technical-error shares and the share of firms where the floor acts. Before the test: the MDE per model is written down, and if model randomness is a large part of the variance of d, the test averages K calls per variant (K fixed before the test)
stability_scope: since 0.4 the repeats cover both arms (full and segment) on the same firms, so the model-noise variance of d itself is estimated as var(d_repeat - d) / 2 on those firms, with its share of var(d); the first pilot's figure (37-38%) used repeats of the full card only and needed assumptions about the segment arm's noise and the dependence of the arms, so it is withdrawn; K (draws per variant averaged in the test) is chosen from the second pilot's estimate before the test; the local model at temperature 0 with a fixed seed is near-deterministic, not exactly (its recorded repeats differ slightly); F1 (since 0.5): r = noise / var(d) with the 80% upper bound of a bootstrap over the repeated firms; K = 1 if the bound < 0.2, 2 if < 0.5, else 3, per model, fixed before the test; since 0.6 var(d) of one draw is the mean of the variances of the two draws, and with fewer than 20 firms with valid repeats of both cards K = 3 (too few for the bound); with K draws a firm-card is a technical error when any of its K draws is (so every part of the report uses one denominator), the sums rule F4 applies to every draw (a draw outside the range makes the firm-card an error in that sensitivity), and the raw sums are reported over all draws; the test averages the band LOG SCORES of the K draws of each card (averaging the distributions would change the measure and is explanatory only). Since 0.7 (project lead's review): K also changes the selection of firms, because a firm-card enters only with all K draws valid, and a model that fails more often loses more firms; the main result is therefore named the mean d among the firms with all K draws of both cards valid (complete cases at the fixed K), and the coverage (firms in the comparison / eligible firms) and the technical-error sensitivities are reported next to it as mandatory; decided by the project lead (18.11.2026): the claim is about the complete cases at the frozen K (does the full card improve the prediction of the SAFE answer among firms for which both cards gave all K valid answers), not extended to all eligible firms or the population; the coverage and the three error sensitivities are mandatory, and if errors_against_the_claim gives a different picture the dependence on missing answers is described. K and the model version are enforced by safe_analyze --frozen on the test split: every run setting of FROZEN_CONFIG (runner version, API, model, base URL, max tokens, context, think, chat template arguments, effort, max attempts, temperature, seed, parser; each must be written, null where it does not apply), the weights digest (local model) or the served model (API, one over every model answer of the run), and K per model; the report records the frozen file's sha256; --average-draws (all designed draws, K differing between firms) is a pilot diagnostic only
exposure: for every model write down the exact dated version id and the stated training cutoff; the 2026Q3 public file was published with the report of 26.10.2026; a cutoff before it rules out memorising the test records, not knowledge of published aggregates or exposure of the development waves; a cheap probe in the pilot: ask the model which survey the question comes from; the 2026Q3 public use file: the date it became available is to be recorded from the download record; the instruction to base a wide distribution on similar firms in Poland can draw on published aggregates, so a model with a cutoff after the 2026Q3 publication carries this as a stated limitation
known_before_freezing: qa21 by wave and size in 2026Q3 (docs/walidacja-safe.md, safe_assumption_check): its test marginals were seen
q0b_3 'don't know' count in the test wave (30; safe_signal_check)
the q0b_3 marginal of the test wave was printed by a domain reviewer on 18.11.2026 (counts only, no records); no recommendation rests on it

the code reviewer (round 1) also printed the counts of q0b_3 by wave including 2026Q3, and a test-split build in the reviewer's scratch directory wrote them to its manifest (counts only, no records; nothing rests on them); since safe_build 0.3 a test-split build records only '1-10', '99' and 'missing'
prompt_tuning: symmetric for the three variants (one system prompt), with a log of versions; the pilot's firms are not evidence

weighted: the mean d weighted with the records' wgtcommon (SAFE economic weights) is reported as explanatory; the estimand is unweighted

development_pilots.first: 120 dev firms, seed 20261118, probabilities prompt (data/processed/safe_dev_pilot_v0.1.json); diagnostic, not evidence
development_pilots.third: decided by the project lead (19.11.2026): a check of the chosen procedure (arm B, chosen by the comparison's rule, without a claim that it forecasts better; the error limit unchanged; no separate arms per model) on new firms: 101 development firms disjoint from both earlier pilots and from the test wave, 30 / 30 / 30 per size class 1-3 and all 11 available firms with 250+ employees (safe_build --sample-by-size 1=30 2=30 3=30 4=11 --exclude-key <pilot 1> <pilot 2>, seed 20261120); the same firms for the three models, with the frozen prompt of arm B (--elicitation counts_nozero), its parser (safe_counts) and the second pilot's settings (safe_analyze --settings-like <the second pilot's report>, the runner version aside); three draws of both cards for every firm (--repeats 2 --repeat-firms 101), 707 items per model, items_sha256 5ff27ec2087862755ac9565baaa3dc4806f43c2ad289de8a1c6016729cd32128 on the code of 0.8 (to be checked after the build); K, coverage and calibration by the procedure so far (two analyses: K from the first, --k-from and --level-check in the second); the forecast of the test sample keeps the test wave's size structure (30/30/30/11 is the pilot's design, not population weights). No further round of prompt changes because a result is weak. If the procedure meets the technical and calibration requirements, the study is frozen whatever the sign of the effect; requirements not met are reported as a limitation, without lowering the criteria automatically. The 11 large firms limit the precision of the diagnostics of that class; reusing earlier firms would not remove that limit and would weaken the independence.
development_pilots.second: 120 fresh dev firms (seed 20261119, the first pilot's firms excluded from evaluation with --exclude-key), counts prompt (zeros allowed); accepted by the project lead (18.11.2026): three draws of both cards (full and segment) for all 120 firms (safe_build --repeats 2 --repeat-firms 120), 840 items per model (120 shuffled, 360 full, 360 segment), items_sha256 956c4192c682393473609571c1befb5bdf94bba45565d7939fe1b8d25558b8d6 on the code of 0.6/0.7 (to be checked after the build); the 320 full and segment items of the earlier 440-item design are among them unchanged, only the donors of the shuffled cards differ; this lets the K rule use 120 firms and the calibration use any K from 1 to 3 (formerly: repeats for 40 firms, A1); a separate comparison of two ways of eliciting the distribution (A3): the 20 repeated firms of pilot 1, the same cards and the same card key, the probabilities instruction vs the counts instruction (they differ in the answer format AND in the instruction, including the rule on zeros, so A3 compares the two elicitations, not the number format alone; --only-repeat-firms-of with the pilot-1 seed); checks: technical errors by variant, raw sums, concentration (entropy, largest share, mass in 1-3) vs pilot 1, noise of d and K, the test's level by tail

h3: since 19.11.2026 exploratory (the project lead's decision): full card vs logit_segment (L2 multinomial logit on size and sector, trained on the development sample, penalty by 4-fold CV on the floored band log-loss); d3 = log score full - log score logit_segment on the firms with a valid full card; estimates and intervals reported, its p shown without any claim; no confirmatory success is declared and no level is passed to H1. (Until 19.11.2026: registered secondary, in the graph with H1.)

elicitation_comparison.status: design decided by the project lead (18.11.2026); the rules on invalid answers, eligibility and the choice decided and accepted for implementation (18.11.2026); fixed before the first call; the calls follow the tests, the implementation review and the blind check of arm B
elicitation_comparison.question: which way of eliciting the distribution to carry into a new development pilot; A vs B tests the zero rule alone, A or B vs C the whole elicitation (instruction and answer format), not the number format alone; no change is assumed to help
elicitation_comparison.firms: the 120 firms of the second pilot (safe_build --only-repeat-firms-of its key.json, seed 20261119), the same records and the same full and segment cards (checked against the second pilot's build)

arms.A: counts per 100 with the current zero rule (the second pilot's instruction, run again)
arms.B: counts per 100 with only the zero rule changed: the first pilot's sentence 'Ocenie, której nie możesz wykluczyć, nie dawaj zera.' instead of the current one; everything else, the parser included, as A
arms.C: probabilities with the first pilot's instruction and answer format (the current card and card key)

elicitation_comparison.items: per model 120 firms x 2 cards (full, segment) x 3 arms x 1 draw = 720 new items, no shuffled cards; 2,160 calls for the three models; one build, the arms interleaved in a seeded random order, each item its own conversation; the same run settings and model versions as the second pilot (checked); the parser named per item (run_b_k2 0.9.4 safe_by_item)
elicitation_comparison.auxiliary: the second pilot's arm-A answers are auxiliary material only (stability of A between runs), not part of the selection
elicitation_comparison.primary_measure: S(arm) = the mean over the three models (equal weights) and the two cards (equal weights) of the mean over the 120 firms of the band log score of the arm (floor 0.01, as in the plan) minus that of the marginal distribution of the training data (the reference; it is the same for every arm, so arms are ranked by their own mean band log score)
elicitation_comparison.invalid_answers: accepted (18.11.2026): an item without a valid answer after max_attempts is scored as the marginal distribution (the fallback a deployed system would use), so every arm is scored on all 120 firms; sensitivities: errors scored worst (floor on the true band) and complete cases common to the three arms
elicitation_comparison.eligibility: decided by the project lead (18.11.2026): an arm with more than 5% technical errors for any model and card is not eligible; if no arm is eligible the result is 'no eligible arm' (no automatic choice; A would not meet the requirement either)
elicitation_comparison.uncertainty_and_ties: decided by the project lead (18.11.2026), a conservative choice under an unresolved difference, not a proof of equivalence or of a tie (Lakens 2017, doi 10.1177/1948550617697177): the paired differences of S for all three pairs of arms (A-B, A-C, B-C) by a bootstrap over firms (2,000 resamples, fixed seed; every resample keeps together all answers of a firm, for every model, card and arm), with family-wise 95% protection for the three pairs (Bonferroni: percentile intervals at 0.05/3 two-sided); an eligible arm is excluded if another eligible arm has a demonstrated advantage over it (the interval of their difference excludes 0 in the other arm's favour); among the remaining eligible arms the smallest change is chosen, in the order A (no change), B (one sentence), C (the whole elicitation); no 'best arm' is picked on the same data
elicitation_comparison.reported_separately_not_ranking: technical errors by model, card and arm and by class; calibration by band (mean predicted vs observed, the largest absolute gap); confident misses (answers giving the true band less than 0.05) and their share of the sum of the log scores; d = full - segment by arm and model, descriptive only, never a selection criterion
elicitation_comparison.not_criteria: the disappearance of zeros (B removes them by its instruction) and d are not selection criteria
elicitation_comparison.after: the chosen arm goes to a new development pilot on fresh firms with its own K and its own calibration before any freezing; the unused development firms number 712, of which 11 have 250+ employees, so that pilot cannot draw 30 per size class (design to be decided)
elicitation_comparison.checks_before_the_calls: pytest; independent code review of the build, the runner change and the comparison script with a mock; a blind check of arm B's prompt; the project lead's approval of the PROPOSED rules

diagnosis_after_pilot_2: decided by the project lead (18.11.2026) after the calibration was not ready (Qwen H3 at 0.0167, n = 650: 52/4000, bound 0.0193): a descriptive diagnosis of the distribution of the H3 differences and of Qwen's technical errors, with a fixed scope run once (safe_analyze --diagnose on the second pilot, first draw, no new model calls): distribution of d and d3 (quantiles, skewness, shares of large losses, the worst 5% of firms), floor hits of the full card, concentration of the answers by variant, technical errors by parser class, raw-text features (aggregates only), repetition across draws, size, sector and true band. Not changed on its result: Qwen and H3 stay in the family, the level criterion and the thresholds stay; no calculation is repeated until it passes; any change of the procedure that follows from the diagnosis is written down first and needs its own calibration before freezing.
level_check: F2 (criterion decided by the project lead, 18.11.2026): before freezing, for every model, H1 (d) and H3 (d3 = full - logit_segment) are checked on their own centred differences from the second pilot (a true null with the observed shape), at two sample sizes fixed here: the expected complete cases in the test (692 x the test share of each size class x the pilot coverage of that class) and all 692 eligible; 4,000 outer replications (fixed seed) and 10,000 inner bootstrap resamples, as in the test (safe_analyze --level-check, defaults --level-reps 4000 --level-inner 10000); rejections in the claim tail (p <= level and mean d > 0, what the graph rejects) at every local level the graph can reach: 0.0167, 0.025 and 0.05. Criterion: the simultaneous one-sided 95% Monte Carlo upper bounds (Clopper-Pearson, Bonferroni over all bounds of the report) do not exceed their local levels. Two flags (since 0.7, the project lead's review): bounds_within_levels (diagnostic, any run) and ready_for_freezing, which also needs the complete declared calibration: all three models of the family, H1 and H3, both sample sizes and the three levels (36 bounds), at least 4,000 outer replications and 10,000 inner resamples, at most 1% replications without a p value, the K planned for the test fixed per model with --k (a result for K = 1 does not approve K = 2 or 3), and development data; --level-check is refused on the test split before any test data is read. Checked by enumerating every rejection sequence of the graph: the local weights of every H1 and H3 are exactly 1/3, 1/2 and 1, so the three levels are complete. A calibration at K > 1 needs K draws of both cards for every firm of the build (--k refuses a build without them). Procedure in two steps (the project lead, 18.11.2026): (1) the first analysis of the second pilot without --level-check, --k and --average-draws; stability.k_rule.recommended_K is read for Qwen, Haiku and Luna separately; (2) the second analysis of all three runs together with --level-check and --k-from <the first report> (K of each model taken from it and checked: same build, same models and served models, the first report on the first draw without --level-check or --k), with the default 4,000 x 10,000; K is not chosen again from the calibration's result; ready_for_freezing requires K from --k-from. The two reports are kept under different names (the first is the basis of the choice of K; the second records the first one's sha256). ready_for_freezing confirms the calibration's conditions only; the freezing also covers the configuration (--frozen), the model versions and the checksums of the materials. 0.0083 (alpha/3 split equally between the tails) is the reference and 0.0125 a diagnostic warning at alpha/3, not a criterion. Not met: the calibration is not sufficiently confirmed (not proof of a faulty test); no automatic correction of the threshold; any change of the procedure needs its own check before freezing. Met: covers the checked scenarios only. In the test the level is not checked again and does not change the decision. Basis of the graphical method: Bretz et al. 2009 and Bretz, Posch, Glimm, Klinglmueller, Maurer, Rohmeyer 2011 (Biometrical Journal 53(6), PMC3427907)
